previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease, hypogammaglobulinemia, and orthostatic hypotension was admitted for evaluation of chest pain and lightheadedness following an IVIG infusion. His symptoms were consistent with prior episodes, occurring in the setting of orthostatic hypotension without evidence of cardiac ischemia, as confirmed by normal serial troponins, unchanged EKG, and recent negative stress test. He was treated with IV hydration, which resolved his orthostatic symptoms. Management focused on preventive strategies, including holding the morning dose of Valsartan on IVIG infusion days and wearing compression stockings. A CH50 level was sent to evaluate for complement activation, with results to be followed up outpatient. He was discharged home in stable condition with no changes to his baseline medications.
